policy: Same-topic prompt similarity >=0.75 and <0.90 requires explicit semantic review bound to the exact prompt texts. A changed prompt invalidates the review.

reviews.reason: UTI is a urinary symptom/upper-tract escalation question; PID tests ascending pelvic infection, fertility consequences, and early treatment. Similarity comes from the generic lead-in, not the assessed knowledge.
UTI evaluates symptom pattern and escalation; the second item evaluates cause-specific therapy, adherence, partner management, and reinfection prevention.
The first tests definitions of labor stages; the second tests delivery mode/position selection using safety, progress, preference, and facility capability.
Labor-stage definitions are separate from indications, contraindications, uterotonic risk, monitoring, and safety systems for induction/augmentation/analgesia.
Physical growth uses longitudinal height/weight/head-circumference trajectories; psychomotor development evaluates multiple developmental domains, change over time, and caregiver observations.

Respiratory-support care evaluates oxygenation, work of breathing, interface skin pressure, and thermal comfort; phototherapy evaluates bilirubin treatment safety, temperature, hydration, elimination, skin, and treatment effect.
One item tests physiologic gastrointestinal/urinary changes; the other tests endocrine, metabolic, and musculoskeletal adaptations. The organ systems and correct principles are different.

Delivery mode/position is shared decision-making around posture and route; induction/augmentation/analgesia tests intervention indications, contraindications, uterotonic risks, monitoring, and facility safety.
The first is post-cesarean wound/discharge danger-sign education; the second is general postpartum graded return to activity, exercise/sexual activity, recovery, and family planning.
